findings.explanation: No Splunk add-on has this name, and Splunkbase app 5380 (cited in dataSources, implementation and references) is 'Mattermost Alerts', an alert-action app that has nothing to do with VMware. The VMware vCenter collection add-on in the grounding guide is the Splunk Add-on for VMware, Splunkbase 3215.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for VMware vSphere Forwarder
findings.suggested_fix: Replace every 'Splunk Add-on for VMware vSphere Forwarder (Splunkbase 5380)' in app, dataSources, implementation, detailedImplementation and references with 'Splunk Add-on for VMware (Splunkbase 3215)'. If the Metrics variant is intended, use 'Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics (Splunkbase 5089)' instead.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for VMware does not emit 'vmware:perf' or 'vmware:vc:event'. It writes performance data to per-group sourcetypes such as vmware:perf:datastore and vmware:perf:disk, and vCenter events to vmware:events. The same wrong names appear in implementation, visualization and detailedImplementation.
findings.quote: sourcetype=vmware:perf and sourcetype=vmware:vc:event for datastore latency and resync or maintenance events
findings.suggested_fix: Use vmware:perf:datastore (and vmware:perf:disk if needed) for latency context, and vmware:events (plus vmware:tasks) for maintenance and resync events. Update the visualization drilldowns and the Step 1 props note to match.

findings.explanation: Get-VsanRuntimeInfo is a cluster-scoped cmdlet. Its only required parameter is -Cluster, so piping a VMHost object to it fails, and the per-host properties the script reads (ResyncIops, TrafficIops, ResyncLatencyUs) are not part of the documented cluster runtime output. dataSources repeats the same claim with 'from Get-VsanRuntimeInfo per host'.
findings.suggested_fix: Call Get-VsanRuntimeInfo -Cluster $cl once per cluster. For per-host resync IOPS and latency, use Get-VsanStat (or the vSAN performance service) and document the actual property names after checking them with Get-Member in a lab.

findings.explanation: The vSAN API and RVC call this per-component attribute bytesToSync, not BytesToResync. If the property name on the PowerCLI VsanResyncingComponent object differs, the poller sends nulls and the whole UC reports zero backlog. The script also reads $row.EntityRuntime.Host.Name and $row.RecoveryETA.TotalSeconds, which may not exist either.
findings.suggested_fix: Run Get-VsanResyncingComponent -Cluster $cl | Get-Member against a supported PowerCLI release and use the real property names for bytes to sync, recovery ETA and owning host in the script and dataSources.

findings.explanation: The poller emits the maintenance state as host_maintenance_mode, but the SPL only coalesces MaintenanceMode, maintenance_mode, VsanMaintenanceMode, vsan_maintenance_mode and EnsureFullDataMigrationMode. maint_mode_list will therefore always be empty, which defeats the runbook step that tells operators to check maint_mode_list before raising a Sev-1.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit the field as maintenance_mode (a name the SPL already reads), or ask the SPL owner to add host_maintenance_mode to the coalesce.

findings.explanation: The Ruby vSphere Console runs on the vCenter Server Appliance, not on ESXi, and Broadcom has deprecated it in favour of PowerCLI, DCLI and the vCenter UI. A reader following this text would look for RVC on ESXi hosts. detailedImplementation repeats 'ESXi RVC snapshots'.
findings.quote: Splunk_TA_nix ingesting ESXi RVC output with sourcetype=vmware:rvc:vsan_resync
findings.suggested_fix: Say RVC runs on the vCenter Server Appliance, mark it as deprecated, or remove the tertiary RVC path.

findings.explanation: The PowerCLI vSphere and vSAN command index lists Get-VsanEnterMaintenanceModeReport and Get-VsanEvacuationPlan but no Get-VsanClusterMaintenanceMode. Get-VsanClusterConfiguration exposing an AdaptiveResyncEnabled property is also unconfirmed, because adaptive resync has not been a user toggle since vSAN 6.7.
findings.quote: When PowerCLI exposes Get-VsanClusterMaintenanceMode on your vCenter build
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm both cmdlet and property names in the PowerCLI reference. If they do not exist, describe how to read the vSAN decommission mode, for example from the vCenter maintenance-mode task or event, and drop or rework the adaptive-resync stream.

findings.explanation: Appendices A to F are one-line placeholders that refer to content that does not exist. Later appendices such as M and N repeat or contradict scope already stated elsewhere. They add length without giving the reader anything to implement.
findings.quote: Appendix E lists forbidden marketing language in internal wiki mirrors of this UC.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete appendices A to F and L. Keep only the material that is specific to this UC (collector sizing in G, poller health in J) and fold it into the Step sections.

findings.explanation: The exclusions field takes ESA clusters out of scope, but the hardware field and Appendix M of detailedImplementation say ESA estates are supported and explain how to mix them with OSA.
findings.quote: Pure vSAN Express Storage Architecture clusters with materially different resync component accounting should carry a dedicated UC
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one scope. Either drop the ESA exclusion, or remove ESA from the hardware field and Appendix M.

findings.explanation: The UC carries status verified with a generic team handle as reviewer. Nothing records an SME sign-off, and the UC contains a wrong Splunkbase ID, wrong sourcetypes and an invalid cmdlet call.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft or community until an SME validates the poller and SPL against a live vSAN cluster.

findings.explanation: This HEC reference URL is truncated and points at the Getting Data In manual root rather than the HTTP Event Collector page.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The search reads every poll in a two-hour window (earliest=-2h@h) and then runs stats sum(bytes_to_resync) BY cluster_id host_id without keeping only the latest poll per component. With the documented one-minute cadence, each component is counted up to about 120 times, so active_resync_gib and the 50 and 200 GiB thresholds apply to an inflated number, and the ETA is skewed by the same summing. latest=@h also snaps the end of the window to the top of the hour, so a */5 schedule ignores up to 59 minutes of the newest data. Fix: dedup or take latest per cluster_id, host_id and component (or use the most recent poll_utc) before summing, and use latest=now.
The maintenance coalesce does not include host_maintenance_mode, which is the field the documented poller emits, so maint_mode_list is always null.

summary: The detailed implementation is well informed about vSAN resync, but the UC names a Splunk add-on that does not exist, cites a Splunkbase ID that belongs to an unrelated app, uses sourcetypes the real VMware add-on does not emit, and gives PowerCLI usage that does not match the cmdlet. The SPL also sums bytes across every poll in a two-hour window, which inflates the backlog figures the thresholds are applied to.
